title: Learning to cook at forty
summary_es: Alguien que aprende a cocinar de adulto. Preposiciones, relativos, tiempos verbales y condicionales.
text: I had never been interested {{1}} cooking. For years I lived on takeaways and whatever my flatmates were kind enough to share. Then, shortly after my fortieth birthday, a friend gave me a cookery course {{2}} a present. I almost didn't go. {{3}} surprised me most on the first evening was how relaxing it felt to chop vegetables after a long day in front of a screen. Our teacher, {{4}} restaurant had closed the year before, was patient and funny, and she never made anyone feel stupid. By the end of the course I {{5}} become confident enough to cook a three-course meal without looking at a recipe. These days I cook almost every evening, and I have even started inviting people round. I'm not saying I will ever {{6}} up takeaways completely, but I no longer depend {{7}} them. If someone had told me this two years ago, I {{8}} not have believed them.

gaps.explanation_es: «Interested in» + nombre o -ing. En español decimos «interesado por/en», pero en inglés siempre es in.
«As a present» = como regalo. «As» indica la función que tiene algo.
«What surprised me most was…» = lo que más me sorprendió fue… «What» equivale aquí a «the thing that».
«Whose» = cuyo: el restaurante es de la profesora. Va seguido directamente del nombre.
«By the end of…» + past perfect: para entonces ya había ocurrido. Después va el participio «become».
«Give up» = dejar, renunciar a algo. Tras «will ever» va el infinitivo sin to.
«Depend on» (más formal: upon). En español es «depender de», y de ahí el error típico «depend of».
Tercera condicional: if + past perfect, would (o might) + have + participio. Habla de un pasado que no ocurrió.
